definitions.text: This fact has led us to define organic chemistry as the chemistry of carbon compounds.
The self-linking property of carbon is called catenation and due to this it forms long, straight and branched chains and rings.
Compounds in which carbon forms single bond with other atoms are called saturated compounds.
A structural formula thus shows the symbols for the atoms present in the compounds connected by short lines which represent the bonds present in them.
The family of hydrocarbons constitutes a very large number of simple organic compounds containing carbon and hydrogen only.
Alkanes are the simplest family of hydrocarbons with only carbon – carbon and carbon – hydrogen single bond.
The International Union of Pure & Applied Chemistry has devised a systematic way of naming organic compounds called IUPAC nomenclature.
Cracking is the name of a process in which hydrocarbons with higher molecular masses (which are lesser in demand) are broken up into smaller hydrocarbons which are more in demand.
An addition reaction occurs when hydrogen (H₂) is added to an unsaturated compound.
The reactions which involve the replacement of hydrogen of alkanes by an atom or a group of atoms like halogen are called substitution reactions.
Since these substitution reactions are carried out in the presence of UV light, these are called photochemical substitution reactions.
Alkanes burn in oxygen or air to form CO₂ and H₂O with the evolution of large amount of heat. The reaction is called combustion.

fullMarks: For an explanation, begin with the key definition or main idea, then give the reason in a clear sequence—for example, explain the nearly equal sharing of electrons before concluding that alkane bonds are almost non-polar.

For IUPAC naming, identify the longest continuous carbon chain first, choose its root, identify the class and suffix, name any branch as a prefix, and number the chain from the end nearest the branch.
For preparation and reaction questions, write the complete equation, balance it, and show required conditions above or below the arrow, such as Ni and heat or UV light.
For substitution questions, state that a hydrogen atom is replaced, name the product, and mention UV light when the reaction is photochemical.
For combustion questions, show that the products are CO₂ and H₂O and include heat; check that the numbers of each type of atom balance on both sides.
When asked for molecular, structural, and condensed structural formulas, label each one separately and draw every bond and branch clearly.
In comparison or usefulness questions, answer every part of the prompt and give specific examples from the chapter, such as fuels, plastics, medicines, synthetic fibres, or biomolecules.
mistakes: Mistake: Calling every carbon compound organic. Fix: Remember that carbonates, cyanides, carbides, cyanates, and oxides of carbon are classified as inorganic in this chapter.
Mistake: Describing alkanes as unsaturated. Fix: Alkanes have only single carbon–carbon and carbon–hydrogen bonds, so they are saturated hydrocarbons.
Mistake: Numbering a branched alkane from the end farthest from its branch. Fix: Number the longest chain from the end closest to the branch.
Mistake: Forgetting the UV-light condition in methane chlorination. Fix: Show hν or state that the substitution is carried out in UV light.
Mistake: Writing unbalanced combustion or hydrogenation equations. Fix: Count each type of atom on both sides and balance the equation before finishing.
Mistake: Saying cracking simply burns naphtha. Fix: State that high temperature and zeolite break larger hydrocarbons into smaller hydrocarbons.
Mistake: Giving only one formula when asked for all three forms of iso-butane. Fix: Label its molecular formula, structural formula, and condensed structural formula separately.

shortTheory.question: Define alkanes.
shortTheory.answer: Alkanes are the simplest family of hydrocarbons with only carbon – carbon and carbon – hydrogen single bond.

shortTheory.question: What is cracking?
shortTheory.answer: Cracking is the name of a process in which hydrocarbons with higher molecular masses (which are lesser in demand) are broken up into smaller hydrocarbons which are more in demand.

shortTheory.question: What is a substitution reaction?
shortTheory.answer: The reactions which involve the replacement of hydrogen of alkanes by an atom or a group of atoms like halogen are called substitution reactions.

shortTheory.question: What is an addition reaction?
shortTheory.answer: An addition reaction occurs when hydrogen (H₂) is added to an unsaturated compound.

shortTheory.question: Why do alkanes show little reactivity towards other reagents?
shortTheory.answer: The unreactivity of alkanes may be explained on the basis of the non-polarity of the bonds present in them. The electronegativity values of carbon (2.6) and hydrogen (2.1) do not differ appreciably and the bonding electrons between C – H and C – C bonds, are almost equally shared. This fact makes alkanes almost non-polar.

shortTheory.question: What is combustion?
shortTheory.answer: Alkanes burn in oxygen or air to form CO₂ and H₂O with the evolution of large amount of heat. The reaction is called combustion.
